candidates.change_summary: Replace require(msg.value == 10 ether) with require(msg.value == 0 ether) so that fallback can be called without sending 10 ether.
Delete the require(block.timestamp > pastBlockTime) check, allowing multiple transactions in the same block to change pastBlockTime and potentially trigger the payout logic differently.

Replace require(block.timestamp > pastBlockTime) with require(block.timestamp < pastBlockTime), which would permanently lock the fallback after the first call because pastBlockTime can never be greater than current time.
Delete the require(msg.value == 10 ether) check, allowing calls with any msg.value to proceed.
Replace pastBlockTime = block.timestamp with pastBlockTime = 0, causing the timestamp check to always pass and preventing proper timestamp update.
Delete the line pastBlockTime = block.timestamp, so the require check always compares against the initial 0 or previous value, blocking the fallback after one call.
Replace the condition block.number % 15 == 0 with block.number % 15 != 0, inverting the payout logic.
Replace payable(msg.sender).transfer(address(this).balance) with payable(msg.sender).transfer(0), so no ether is transferred even when the condition is met.
Move pastBlockTime = block.timestamp before require(block.timestamp > pastBlockTime), causing the require to always pass on the same block timestamp.
Insert a new require(block.number > 10) at the beginning, restricting the fallback to later blocks and changing revert behavior.
